name: rag_papers_v1
description: 20 questions over four RAG papers (RAG 2005.11401, DPR 2004.04906, GraphRAG 2404.16130, Self-RAG 2310.11511). Evidence labels were written from the indexed chunk text and are validated against the collection before every run.

questions.question: Which retriever does the RAG model use?
questions.reference_answer: RAG's retriever is based on DPR (Dense Passage Retrieval), a bi-encoder whose query and document encoders are both BERT-base models.

questions.question: What generator model does RAG use, and how many parameters does it have?
questions.reference_answer: RAG uses BART-large, a pre-trained seq2seq transformer with 400M parameters, as its generator.

questions.question: What document index does RAG retrieve from?
questions.reference_answer: A December 2018 Wikipedia dump split into disjoint 100-word chunks (21M documents), embedded with the DPR document encoder and stored in a FAISS MIPS index with HNSW approximation.

questions.question: How much does DPR improve over BM25 in top-20 passage retrieval accuracy?
questions.reference_answer: DPR outperforms a strong Lucene-BM25 system by 9%-19% absolute in top-20 passage retrieval accuracy.

questions.question: Which community detection algorithm does GraphRAG use to build its graph communities?
questions.reference_answer: GraphRAG uses Leiden community detection, applied hierarchically to recursively find sub-communities until leaf communities cannot be partitioned further.

questions.question: What are reflection tokens in Self-RAG?
questions.reference_answer: Special tokens the language model generates alongside its output; they are categorized into retrieval tokens, signalling whether retrieval is needed, and critique tokens, judging the quality of the generation.

questions.question: What is index hot-swapping in RAG?
questions.reference_answer: Because RAG's knowledge lives in a non-parametric index, knowledge can be updated at test time by replacing the document index (e.g. swapping a 2016 Wikipedia index for a 2018 one) without retraining, unlike parametric-only models such as T5 or BART.

questions.question: How did RAG perform on FEVER fact verification?
questions.reference_answer: For 3-way FEVER classification RAG scores within 4.3% of state-of-the-art pipeline models, which use domain-specific architectures and intermediate retrieval supervision that RAG does not need.

questions.question: What is the difference between RAG-Sequence and RAG-Token?
questions.reference_answer: RAG-Sequence uses the same retrieved document to generate the whole output sequence, marginalizing over the top-K documents per sequence; RAG-Token can use a different latent document for each generated token, so the generator can draw on several documents within one answer.

contains: different latent document for each target token

questions.question: Compare how RAG and Self-RAG decide when to retrieve passages.
questions.reference_answer: RAG always retrieves the top-K documents with its retriever for every input. Self-RAG trains the model to retrieve adaptively, on demand, signalled by reflection tokens, and criticizes approaches that retrieve a fixed number of passages indiscriminately.

questions.question: How does GraphRAG compare with vector RAG on global sensemaking questions?
questions.reference_answer: Vector RAG retrieves records close to the query in embedding space and struggles with global questions about a whole corpus. GraphRAG builds an entity graph index with hierarchical community summaries and shows substantial improvements over a vector RAG baseline in comprehensiveness and diversity of answers.

questions.question: How does RAG use DPR, and how was the DPR retriever trained?
questions.reference_answer: RAG initializes its retriever and builds its document index with a pre-trained DPR bi-encoder that was trained to retrieve documents containing answers to TriviaQA and Natural Questions. DPR trains its question and passage encoders with in-batch negatives (other questions' positive passages in the mini-batch serve as negatives), plus BM25 hard negatives.

questions.question: Which papers in the collection use BERT-based dense encoders for retrieval, and how?
questions.reference_answer: DPR uses two independent BERT-base (uncased) networks as question and passage encoders and takes the [CLS] representation (d = 768). RAG's retriever follows DPR's bi-encoder architecture with BERT-base query and document encoders.

questions.question: What limitations of standard retrieval-augmented generation does Self-RAG identify?
questions.reference_answer: Standard RAG indiscriminately retrieves and incorporates a fixed number of passages regardless of whether retrieval is needed or the passages are relevant, which diminishes versatility and can produce unhelpful or low-quality outputs; and its outputs are not guaranteed to be consistent with the retrieved passages.

contains: indiscriminately retrieving and incorporating a fixed number

questions.question: What limitations of its evaluation does the GraphRAG paper report?
questions.reference_answer: The evaluation only covers sensemaking questions over two corpora of roughly 1 million tokens each, so generalization to other domains and use cases is unknown, and fabrication rates were not compared (e.g. with SelfCheckGPT).

questions.question: What retriever, generator and knowledge source does RAG combine?
questions.reference_answer: A DPR-based bi-encoder retriever, a BART-large generator (400M parameters), and a non-parametric memory of 21M 100-word Wikipedia chunks indexed with FAISS.

questions.question: What criteria and which datasets does GraphRAG use for its evaluation?
questions.reference_answer: LLM-evaluated head-to-head criteria of comprehensiveness, diversity, empowerment and directness, on two datasets of about 1 million tokens: podcast transcripts and news articles.
